exposure: Dexmedetomidine hydrochloride (Dex) combined with bupivacaine hydrochloride for intraoperative anesthesia and Dex + ropivacaine hydrochloride for postoperative analgesia
Bupivacaine hydrochloride for intraoperative anesthesia and morphine + ropivacaine hydrochloride for postoperative analgesia (control)
outcome: Postoperative analgesia (Visual Analogue Scale - VAS scores)
Cognitive function (Montreal Cognitive Assessment - MoCA, Mini-Mental State Examination - MMSE scores)
cohort: One hundred and two pregnant women undergoing cesarean section in People's Hospital of Zhangqiu District from August 2016 to July 2017.
finding: The use of Dexmedetomidine hydrochloride (Dex) in cesarean section anesthesia resulted in more stable hemodynamics, better postoperative analgesia, and reduced incidence of postoperative agitation, transient neurological syndrome (TNS), and cognitive dysfunction compared to the control group.
